blocks.label: Squat, leg raises in the rest
blocks.why: The back squat first, at a weight you trust for eight to twelve: muscle grows as well on twelve good reps as on five heavy ones, and depth is what works the glutes. Add reps until all three sets reach twelve, then add weight. The leg raises ride in its rest on the bar above the rack.

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Feet a little wider than hips, toes slightly out. Set a box behind you at a depth you trust. Breathe in and hold it, brace your stomach, then sit down between your feet until you just touch the box; never sit on it. Knees push out over your second toe. Fresh breath every rep. When every set feels solid, use a lower box. Stop when a rep looks different.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Lighter than the back squat. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Fingertips just hook under the bar; the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. Because the bar is in front, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier. If the elbows drop the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Hang from the bar, hands shoulder width, shoulders pulled down away from your ears. Brace your stomach, then lift your legs nearly straight until your feet reach hip height, curling your hips up at the top. Lower over two seconds without swinging. When ten clean reps are easy, lift higher.

alts.name: Hanging Knee Raise
alts.cue: Hang from the bar on top of the rack, arms straight, feet clear of the floor. Bring both knees up toward your chest, and at the top keep going a couple of inches by curling your hips under you. That last bit is the part your abdominals do. Lower under control until your legs are straight and you have come to a STOP before the next rep. No swinging. When fifteen is easy, straighten the legs instead of adding weight.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

exercises.whyHere: the leg raises ride in its rest on the bar above the rack

blocks.label: Step-up, triceps extension in the rest
blocks.why: One leg at a time, the step-up you asked for: each glute does its own work, which a squat cannot make it do. The overhead triceps extension rides in its rest, seated on the end of the same bench, for the back of the arm the presses barely stretch.

exercises.name: DB Step-Up
exercises.cue: Box or bench at knee height, a dumbbell in each hand. Put your whole foot on top and drive up through that HEEL until you stand tall on it. The foot on the floor does not push off: lift it like a passenger. Lower slowly on the same leg. All reps on one leg, then the other. Success: your knee tracks over your toes and the top hip does not drop.

firstWeight.say: First try: start with 30 lb dumbbells and work up until 8 a leg feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

alts.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Sit on the end of the bench, back tall, one dumbbell held in both hands above your head, arms straight. Bend only at the elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch in the back of your arms, elbows pointing up and staying close. Straighten back up. Upper arms stay still the whole set.
exercises.whyHere: The overhead triceps extension rides in its rest, seated on the end of the same bench

blocks.label: Incline press, lateral raise in the rest
blocks.why: Your low-incline dumbbell press, chest being a weak point you named. The lateral raise rides in its rest, standing beside the bench, for the sides of the shoulders.

exercises.name: DB Incline Press
exercises.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat. Shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, pause one second, press up over your lower chest. Success: a stretch across the chest at the bottom, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder.

alts.name: BB Bench Press
alts.cue: Flat bench inside the rack. Set the safety pins at chest height BEFORE you load the bar, every time, because you train alone. Feet flat, grip a little wider than your shoulders, shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower to your lower chest until it touches lightly, press up, same spot every rep. If you have to bounce it, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: A press on a machine, moderate rather than heavy: the barbell bench is where the press gets pushed. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if pouring from two jugs. Lower about twice as slowly as you lifted. Success: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top. If either fails, go lighter.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

exercises.whyHere: The lateral raise rides in its rest, standing beside the bench

blocks.label: One-arm row, single-leg RDL in the rest
blocks.why: The one-arm row with the bench set flat again: a pull to match the press, one arm then the other. The single-leg RDL rides in its rest, the back of each leg on its own with one dumbbell and the only hamstring work in this session.

exercises.name: DB Single-Arm Row
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Same bench as the press, set flat for this. One knee and the same-side hand on the bench, the other foot on the floor, back flat. Dumbbell hanging straight down. Pull it to your hip by driving the ELBOW back past your ribs, pause, lower all the way until the shoulder stretches. All reps on one arm, then the other. Your back does not twist to lift it.

firstWeight.say: First try: start with a 50 lb dumbbell and work up until 8 an arm feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

alts.name: BB Row
alts.cue: Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS back past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Same bar as the bench: change the plates, not the rack. If you have to stand up to move the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Same bench as the press, one notch steeper, lying face down with your chest on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand. Pull your elbows back past your ribs and squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower until the arms are straight. The bench holds your back still, so nothing can cheat.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL
exercises.cue: One dumbbell, in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg, the other hand on a bench or rack. Soft standing knee, push the hips back and let the free leg travel straight back as the dumbbell lowers down the standing shin. Stop when that hamstring pulls; do not chase the floor. Hips stay level. Holding on is the point: your hamstring decides the weight, not your balance.

alts.name: DB RDL
alts.cue: Both feet down, a dumbbell in each hand: the same hinge without the balance. Use it on a day one leg feels off.

exercises.whyHere: The single-leg RDL rides in its rest

blocks.label: Bound sideways
blocks.why: Two sets of three bounds each side, between your warm-up sets, while you are fresh.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.cue: Three bounds a side, then stop. Stand on your LEFT leg, push off sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over the toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and hold. Silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Box Jump
alts.cue: Three jumps a set, then stop. You are training how fast you leave the floor, and a tired jump is a slow one. Stand a forearm length from the box, swing the arms back, bend the knees a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. STEP down, never jump down. A thud, or a third jump slower than the first, means the box is too high.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Lateral Line Hop
alts.cue: The easier version. Both feet together, hop side to side over a line on the floor, small and fast, staying on the balls of your feet. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.

blocks.label: Romanian deadlift, curl in the rest
blocks.why: The heavy hinge, at your own six to eight: the back of the legs and the glutes. The curl rides in its rest, standing tall, for the front of the arm that rows and pull-ups only reach second-hand.

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar touches your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and FREEZE them, then push your hips back toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and drive the hips forward to stand. If your lower back rounds you went too far. Straps are fine.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

alts.name: Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: One dumbbell, in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with a soft knee, push the hips back and let the free leg travel straight back behind you as the dumbbell lowers down the standing shin. Stop when the hamstring of the standing leg pulls; do not chase the floor. Success: your hips stay level, no rolling open to the side. Hold the rack with your free hand if you wobble, that is not cheating. 8/leg.

exercises.name: DB Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Curl up, squeeze at the top, lower slowly all the way.

alts.name: DB Hammer Curl
alts.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs the whole way, like holding two hammers. Curl both up together until the dumbbells reach shoulder height, elbows staying at your sides, then lower slowly. Your torso does not rock. If your elbows drift forward or your back leans, go lighter.

alts.name: Incline DB Curl
alts.cue: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

exercises.whyHere: The curl rides in its rest, standing tall

blocks.label: Hip thrust, reverse fly in the rest
blocks.why: The glute lift, on the Smith so the bar runs on rails while you learn the position. The reverse fly rides in its rest, for the backs of the shoulders that hold your posture.

exercises.name: Smith Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: DRAFT, tell the note box what is wrong with it. Bar low on the rails, a pad on your hip crease, upper back on a bench, feet flat about one and a half shoulder widths apart. Drive your hips up until your shins are vertical and your thighs level with the floor, no higher: ribs stay down. One second up, two seconds down, hips brush the floor between reps.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

firstWeight.say: First try: start at 70 lb of plates (not counting the Smith bar) and work up until 10 reps feels hard, about 2 left in the tank. Log that weight.

exercises.name: DB Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Open your arms out to the SIDES like opening curtains until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Your torso does not rise. Go light, this is a small muscle.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the adjustable cable column, standing tall, a handle in each hand and a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

exercises.whyHere: The reverse fly rides in its rest

blocks.label: Vertical pull
blocks.why: The pull for this session, placed before any carrying so your hands can still hold on.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

alts.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Loop a band over the bar on top of the rack, pull one end through the other, and put one knee in the loop. Hands a little wider than your shoulders. Pull your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin is over the bar, then lower slowly to straight arms. Same band every time; when 10 is easy, use a lighter band.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight.

blocks.label: Chest press and farmer carry
blocks.why: The machine chest press, chest in both sessions without the same dumbbell press four times a week, and the machine steadies the shoulder. The farmer carry takes turns with it, last, when the grip has nothing left to do.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.cue: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest. Back flat on the pad, feet flat. Press the handles forward until your arms are straight but not locked, then let them come back under control until you feel the stretch across your chest. Shoulders stay down and back against the pad the whole set.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat. Shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, pause one second, press up over your lower chest. Success: a stretch across the chest at the bottom, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: A heavy dumbbell in each hand. Stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after. Start the watch before you pick them up, because both hands are full. Count seconds and type the seconds. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, and THE RACK STOPS AT 50 LB EACH: that is the whole set, 20 up to 50, two of each. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

exercises.whyHere: The farmer carry takes turns with it, last
